Every combination of an X value and a Y value is a pair.
code.python:

Y = ['Low', 'High']
pairs = [(x, y) for x in X for y in Y]

code.pseudocode: Each pair is one cell of the table.
code.python:
X = [1, 2, 3]

code.pseudocode: P(X = x, Y = y) is stored for every pair, and all of them add up to 1.
If X and Y were unrelated, P(x, y) would equal P(x) * P(y). Compare.
code.python:
joint = {
    (1, 'Low'): 0.25, (1, 'High'): 0.05,
    (2, 'Low'): 0.20, (2, 'High'): 0.20,
    (3, 'Low'): 0.05, (3, 'High'): 0.25,
}
p_x3 = joint[(3, 'Low')] + joint[(3, 'High')]
p_high = sum(p for (x, y), p in joint.items() if y == 'High')
print(round(p_x3 * p_high, 2), joint[(3, 'High')])   # 0.15 0.25: more than chance alone
